title: The Operationalization Gap: Where Safety Objectives Stop Becoming Deployment Practices

original_idea.body:
# The Operationalization Gap: Where Safety Objectives Stop Becoming Deployment Practices

**Problem:** Operationalization chain: 'high-level safety objective' (e.g., 'prevent CBRN uplift') -> 'measurable criterion' -> 'concrete deployment practice' -> 'enforced at inference'. Translating objectives into practice is a named open problem; the objective-to-measurable-criterion link is where vague goals fail to become testable.

**Direction:** Take 5-6 commonly stated safety objectives from public frameworks and trace each through published documentation to see how far it becomes operational: stated goal / named metric / concrete deployment guardrail / monitored in production. Quantify where in the chain each objective stalls and which objectives never reach a measurable criterion.

**Why it matters:** Practical operationalization methods are explicitly listed as an open problem. Showing which safety objectives never become measurable tells the field where the conceptual-to-operational translation work is most urgently missing. Document analysis only, no compute, strong counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in Technical AI Governance (operationalization as open problem); Anthropic RSP CBRN thresholds; OpenAI Preparedness tracked risk categories; FLI AI Safety Index.
